source.scope: All 17 printed CCPh ASOP steps and identified supplemental in-volume families. Campaign/module/equipment profiles need their own reconciliation.

options.title: Finish one Location before starting the next
options.prompt: Which Location does the ATTACKER select, and what remains unresolved there?
checks: The ATTACKER chooses the order of CC Locations. Complete that Location’s opening, declarations, attacks, withdrawals and closing status before starting another.
Keep phase-wide aerial combat, Clearance and cleanup in a separate queue, even when no ground CC exists.
A reference Considered mark performs no game action. A live phase cannot close while committed attacks or required effects remain unresolved.
options.effect: Propose a Location queue, a declaration receipt and a separate end-phase obligations queue.
options.example: Resolving one village fight does not permit TI cleanup while another Location still has attacks.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.
options.timing: Rule-specific CCPh timing; supplemental to ASOP

options.title: Identify the actual combat participants
options.prompt: Which opposing units can legally engage each other?
checks: Use Location, level and terrain status rather than just hex membership. Foxhole occupants can fight other units in the same Location; separate building levels normally cannot.
Apply pillbox’s same-hex exception, cave restrictions and non-frozen Ocean prohibition before showing attacks.
Carry forward concealment, PIN, TI, CX, broken status, equipment, mounted status, prior Melee and earlier phase history without silently clearing them.
options.effect: Show separate combat groups and explain why apparent neighbors cannot attack.
options.example: Opposing units on different floors do not automatically fight because their counters share a hex.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.
options.timing: Rule-specific CCPh timing; supplemental to ASOP

options.title: Place hidden items and disclose concealed strengths
options.prompt: What must become visible at this Location’s opening?
checks: Place the Location’s hidden items onboard under concealment and reveal concealed Strength Factors; remove Dummies before attack designation.
Revealing strength is not blanket loss of concealment. Retain the remaining protection until a specific loss trigger.
Do not reveal every CC Location simultaneously when only one has been selected; respect special pillbox inspection and other profile rules.
options.effect: Separate public strength disclosure from concealment removal.
options.example: A concealed squad’s strength becomes known while its concealment still affects the coming attack.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Resolve a revealed hidden Tank-Hunter Hero
options.prompt: Does involuntary revelation meet the hero’s survival exception?
checks: A hidden T-H Hero involuntarily revealed in CCPh survives this special test only as a DEFENDER in the same Location with an enemy AFV.
Apply its special target and attack obligations if it remains; do not treat it as an ordinary Hero with a general heroic DRM.
options.effect: Resolve the special revealed-counter consequence before offering attacks.
options.example: A hidden T-H Hero revealed without the qualifying AFV cannot remain as ordinary Infantry.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Determine whether Ambush applies
options.prompt: Is this a new encounter with a qualifying terrain or concealment trigger?
checks: Check Infantry advance into woods/building or by/against concealed units, and the hidden-unit placement trigger. Jungle, bamboo and kunai qualify under G.6.
Reinforcing an existing Melee does not create a fresh ordinary Ambush roll. A vehicle in the Location does not by itself prevent Ambush.
Normally one side must roll at least three lower after drm; the unilluminated night ATTACKER uses the E1.77 two-lower exception.
options.effect: Explain the trigger and threshold before either side rolls.
options.example: An unilluminated night attacker can gain Ambush with a two-point advantage.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Build each side’s Ambush modifier explanation
options.prompt: Which qualifying units and statuses contribute to the Ambush dr?
checks: Account for concealment, Stealth/Lax, CX, broken, pinned, berserk, vehicle/Cavalry/pillbox, BU/Stun, bank/Panji and PTO attacker conditions.
Apply the best eligible unpinned Good Order leader with the alone/berserk restrictions. Do not substitute CC attack DRM for Ambush drm.
Retain relevant force-wide qualifiers even when only part of the force has the status; keep hidden identities private until lawful disclosure.
options.effect: Show one auditable dr calculation per side.
options.example: A concealed Stealthy squad with a CX leader has both favorable and unfavorable Ambush modifiers.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Use the Ambush advantage or withdraw
options.prompt: Attack first, leave before combat, or preserve a later withdrawal option?
checks: The ambusher normally resolves all its attacks first; apply the sequential-priority rules when prisoners are involved. The ambushed side loses concealment.
Eligible unpinned, non-berserk, non-Disrupted Infantry may withdraw before resolution or after all attacks by and against it, before Melee.
An attacking ambusher can retain concealment when it eliminates/captures its target. An unsuccessful attack loses that special protection.
options.effect: Expose the two distinct withdrawal windows and the consequence of attacking.
options.example: An ambusher can leave safely now instead of risking a failed attack and return attack.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Check Street Fighting without inventing an Ambush roll
options.prompt: Does the earlier advance or Bypass position qualify against this vehicle?
checks: Check the road with buildings on both sides and ground-level advance provenance, or eligible Infantry in the vehicle’s Bypassed obstacle.
The special -1/+1 vehicle-combat advantage does not stack with actual Ambush; actual Ambush takes precedence.
Preserve the eligible return-to-origin option after attacks, with broken/pinned/above-Wire restrictions and return hazards. It is not a general free Withdrawal.
options.effect: Keep actual Ambush, Street Fighting modifiers and the later return decision separate.
options.example: A Street Fighter on top of Wire receives the applicable combat benefit but cannot return to its building.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Consider DEFENDER Tank-Hunter Hero creation
options.prompt: Can a qualifying Japanese squad or HS create a hero here?
checks: Require an armed Good Order Japanese Infantry squad/HS with an enemy AFV in the same Location and LOS, no disqualifying fire/Pin/TI marker, and remaining scenario allowance.
Wait for Ambush determination and completion of all ATTACKER Ambush attacks. The printed opening step does not override that explicit delay.
Apply the creation dr and HS/Conscript/DC modifiers, Original 6 Pin consequence and Designated Target choice. The hero must attempt to attack that AFV if still in its Location.
options.effect: Queue the choice after any required attacker Ambush attacks rather than resolving it prematurely.
options.example: An ambushed Japanese squad must survive the attacker’s attacks before attempting creation.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Choose the correct attack sequence
options.prompt: Which rule decides who attacks next?
checks: Vehicle presence, even an abandoned vehicle not being attacked, creates sequential CC. The non-vehicular side starts; if both sides have vehicles, the ATTACKER starts.
Ambush normally gives the ambusher all its attacks first. Prisoner attacks take priority when the higher-numbered sequential rule applies.
Show the precedence explicitly. In ordinary vehicle sequence alternate one attack at a time, recomputing survivors and escorts after each result.
options.effect: Display current decision owner, governing rule and the next available attack window.
options.example: Prisoners can attack before other combatants even in a Location with both Ambush and a vehicle.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Declare eligible prisoner escape attacks
options.prompt: Can these prisoners attack their Guard now?
checks: Outside Melee the Guard must be broken and prisoners must pass an NTC. In existing Melee the NTC and broken-Guard conditions no longer apply.
Only eligible Infantry may escape; apply Italian, Japanese and Axis Minor restrictions and the specified Axis Minor exception.
The Guard must be eliminated before attacking others unless included in the same attack. Mere Guard elimination does not guarantee freedom if other enemies remain.
options.effect: Show eligible escape groups, required checks and the conditions for actual freedom.
options.example: Prisoners in established Melee can attack an unbroken Guard without another NTC.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Declare an escorted abandoned-vehicle capture attempt
options.prompt: Is this vehicle contested or eligible for later automatic capture?
checks: An abandoned AFV with enemy Personnel present requires a CC capture attempt; both sides may contest it and supply its escort protection until controlled.
Treat the unmanned AFV as CE and Immobile and apply the no-manned-MG modifier. A manned AFV cannot be captured by this procedure.
If no enemy Personnel remain, the automatic capture window is at Location close. Do not award ownership at the opening merely because the vehicle is abandoned.
options.effect: Distinguish attack commitment from the possible automatic closing result.
options.example: Two opposing squads beside an abandoned tank must resolve the contest before assigning its crew.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Declare voluntary Withdrawal from Melee
options.prompt: Which eligible units leave, and which stand to cover them?
checks: ATTACKER declares first, before either side’s attacks. Ordinary Withdrawal requires existing Melee and excludes pinned, berserk and Disrupted units.
Withdrawing units cannot attack, and declarations cannot be canceled after seeing combat results. Apply the -2 target DRM plus standing-friendly-unit protection.
SMC departing without a MMC can be singled out. Apply withdrawal modifiers only to withdrawing targets in a mixed attack.
options.effect: Commit separate standing and withdrawing groups before attack selection.
options.example: A leader can withdraw while a squad stands, but may then be attacked as a separate target.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Handle compulsory broken-unit Withdrawal
options.prompt: Which broken Infantry must attempt to leave Melee?
checks: Non-Disrupted, non-Guard broken Infantry must attempt Withdrawal. Broken units never attack but defend with their full unbroken-side FP and the broken-unit DRM.
Apply the special Failure-to-Rout consequence for a non-Guard broken unit unable to withdraw at Location close; preserve the Disrupted/Guard distinctions.
After successful Withdrawal, normal rout rules apply in a subsequent RtPh. This is not an extra rout now.
options.effect: Show compulsory declaration and any unresolved closing consequence separately.
options.example: A broken squad cannot choose to remain in Melee simply because its retreat looks dangerous.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Drop excess equipment and evaluate an Accessible exit
options.prompt: What can this withdrawing unit retain, and where can it legally go?
checks: Retained equipment cannot exceed IPC; offer the legal opening drop instead of refusing every overburdened unit outright.
Destination must be Accessible under normal advance conditions, possibly creating CX, and cannot contain a Known enemy. Terrain and pillbox restrictions still apply.
Entering a real concealed enemy’s Location eliminates the withdrawing unit and forces the prescribed enemy reveal; do not disclose that hidden risk in a public destination list.
Infantry above a Panji counter cannot Withdraw from CC off that counter. A generic Accessible-hex test must not bypass this explicit prohibition.
options.effect: Show load choices and viewer-safe endpoints without claiming unknown destinations are safe.
options.example: A squad drops an HMG to meet IPC, but an unseen enemy can still make its chosen exit fatal.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Declare SMC solo status and defending groups
options.prompt: Which unit does each SMC attack and defend with?
checks: ATTACKER establishes pairing/solo status first, before attack declarations. Each SMC contributes one FP in ordinary Personnel CC.
A solo attacker also defends alone. A paired SMC attacks with its MMC if combining, and normally cannot be singled out separately.
A Known SMC cannot defend with a concealed unit without resolving the required concealment compatibility; withdrawal can create separate targetability.
options.effect: Make defensible groups visible before targeting, and lock them at the proper point.
options.example: Pairing a leader with a squad changes both the attack and the smallest target the opponent can select.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Choose eligible leadership and heroic support
options.prompt: Who may direct this declared attack?
checks: One leader can direct the attack of the group it defends with and other units joining that combined attack. No leadership DRM for a solo leader or an attack with berserk units.
For a vehicle target the leader must combine in that attack; apply the separate CCV combination limit. Heroic effects are distinct, and a T-H Hero supplies no ordinary Hero DRM.
CC does not generate LLMC/LLTC from leader casualties. Do not queue a generic leader-loss check.
options.effect: Show FP/CCV contribution separately from the attack modifier.
options.example: A solo 9-2 leader does not get to apply its -2 leadership to its own attack.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Declare targets at the correct commitment boundary
options.prompt: Which attacks must be fixed now, and which can wait?
checks: In simultaneous CC the ATTACKER declares all attacks, then DEFENDER declares all, before resolution. Preserve each declared strength even if its units are simultaneously lost.
Sequential CC declares the next attack after prior effects; no eliminated unit gets a later return attack. Passing and exhausted attackers must be tracked.
Units need not all attack or all be attacked. Enforce ordinary once-per-unit attack/target limits with vehicle and special-rule exceptions.
options.effect: Provide a commitment review rather than letting the player retarget after a favorable die roll.
options.example: An eliminated squad still resolves its declared simultaneous attack, but not a future sequential one.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Choose whether concealed units attack
options.prompt: Keep concealment or commit it to an attack?
checks: Resolve the concealed participant’s attack/decline intent before final attack odds and targets depend on it; do not let declaration order provide a concealment trap.
Making or directing an attack normally loses concealment, with successful Ambush retention as the explicit exception. Attack FP against a concealed target is halved.
A unit retaining concealment is neither held in Melee nor able to hold opponents in Melee. A casualty can change that status.
options.effect: Compare attack now with retaining concealment and later freedom of movement.
options.example: A concealed defender can decline its attack, leaving the attacker facing reduced odds.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Build ordinary Personnel CC odds
options.prompt: Combine or split the attack, and which defending group is the target?
checks: Use eligible inherent FP, including SMC groups, and round the odds down to a printed CCT column. Ordinary SW/Guns do not add attack FP.
Apply applicable Pin, Guard, concealment, CX, TI, broken-target, withdrawal, Ambush and stacking effects at their proper calculation stages.
No PBF/TPBF, TEM or LOS Hindrance modifies ordinary CC. Keep different target DRM separate rather than assigning one result to an unlike group.
options.effect: Show strength arithmetic, odds, Kill Number and target-specific modifiers before commitment.
options.example: Two squads may combine against one defender or split attacks, with different odds and risks.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Choose or require Hand-to-Hand under the active profile
options.prompt: Does this nationality, Deluxe rule or SSR permit or require HtH?
checks: HtH is not a universal toggle. Deluxe/SSR ATTACKER permissions, Gurkha choice, Japanese automatic conditions and Dare-Death rules differ; respect Ambush, Pin and Withdrawal exceptions.
Use red Kill Numbers for eligible Personnel combat and retain HtH for the continuing Melee. Vehicle/PRC/pillbox attacks do not acquire HtH benefits.
Japanese/Gurkha qualifying HtH attacks receive their extra modifier. Mixed vehicle Locations still require separate eligible Personnel and vehicle procedures.
options.effect: Show the enabling profile, whether optional or mandatory, and which attacks it affects.
options.example: Japanese eligible attacking Infantry may require HtH while an AFV in the same Location still uses its own procedure.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Declare capture instead of elimination
options.prompt: Is capture legal for this attacker and target, and worth the changed modifier?
checks: A non-vehicular, non-berserk attacker must predesignate capture against a permitted target; manned AFV and Motion/non-stopped vehicle restrictions apply.
Normal capture adds +1, replaced by -1 against Inexperienced Personnel. Mixed target classes can yield different results from the same roll.
Below the Kill Number captures all affected defenders; equality captures one defender-selected unit or a HS of a squad. No Quarter does not replace these rules with a generic execute option.
options.effect: Keep attack mode and target-specific capture results in the declaration receipt.
options.example: A Partial Kill capture lets the defender select the captured unit rather than using ordinary casualty Random Selection.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Build a Personnel attack against a vehicle
options.prompt: Which unit and optional SMC make this vehicle attack?
checks: Use CCV: squad 5, crew 4, HS 3, SMC 2, with applicable Assault Engineer, Inexperienced and halving penalties.
At most two units combine, one a SMC adding one to the other unit’s CCV. Do not sum several squads or mix Personnel and vehicle targets in one attack.
Evaluate current escort, Motion/non-stopped, armor/exposure, immobility and manned functioning MG modifiers at this attack, plus valid leadership/hero/Ambush/Street Fighting effects.
options.effect: Display the vehicle attack’s CCV and modifiers separately from Personnel odds.
options.example: Eliminating an escort in an earlier sequential attack can improve the next attack on the tank.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Allocate eligible vehicle CC weapons
options.prompt: Which functioning armament can attack, separately or together?
checks: Check eligible AAMG, unrestricted CMG, RMG, turreted MA IFE ≤15mm and allowed halftrack passenger fire. A BMG is not a CC weapon.
Vehicle FP forms CCT odds against Personnel CCV, using black Kill Numbers. Apply cumulative halving and Shock/Stun limits; no ROF or Intensive Fire sequence is created.
Weapons may combine or make separate legal attacks. Track each used weapon and target exceptions instead of spending one generic vehicle attack.
options.effect: Show available weapon allocations with their own consumed status.
options.example: A tank can use its sN separately and still have an eligible CMG attack later in the sequence.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Handle Riders, Passengers and vehicle capture targets
options.prompt: Can these occupants be attacked separately or only with their vehicle?
checks: Riders may be attacked separately with their own attack/defense modifiers. Other PRC normally share vehicle destruction, with no survival roll in CC.
For capturing an eligible stationary unarmored vehicle, all other enemy Personnel must be eliminated/captured and its Passengers captured through the special Personnel CC procedure.
Apply passenger attack/defense and capture modifiers; do not offer capture of a manned AFV or Motion/non-stopped vehicle.
options.effect: Separate Rider targets, special Passenger capture and vehicle-wide consequences.
options.example: Destroying an AFV in CC eliminates its PRC without a crew-survival choice.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Consider the separate sN close-defense attack
options.prompt: Is this equipped AFV eligible to use its close-defense projector now?
checks: Require the correct equipment/date and BU status. Normally the AFV or escort must already have been attacked this CCPh; a qualifying ambusher has an exception.
Use a separate 16-FP IFT attack on every unarmored unit in the Location, including friendly units and vulnerable PRC. Never combine it with MG FP.
Apply its Original-DR Usage Number test and special CC modifiers, without ordinary TEM/SMOKE. Do not add the usual BU smoke-dispenser usage penalty to this HE attack.
options.effect: Preview friendly exposure and the exact eligibility trigger before commitment.
options.example: A tank can hurt its own escort with sN, so the choice belongs beside the target consequences.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Apply pillbox, sewer, cave and obstacle exceptions
options.prompt: Does the terrain change attack eligibility, modifiers or continuing Melee?
checks: Pillbox CC crosses its separate Location boundary only under B30.6; friendly outside units can block it, vehicle/PRC versus occupants is barred, and HtH/Melee do not result.
Sewer concealment prevents ordinary Melee lock. Units inside a cave cannot conduct CC with units outside it.
Apply above-Wire, Panji and bank status consequences to their actual subjects. Do not reintroduce general terrain TEM into CC.
options.effect: Explain terrain-specific targeting and post-combat status.
options.example: Pillbox occupants and outside Infantry may fight yet remain outside ordinary Melee afterward.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Apply mounted and water-combat profiles
options.prompt: Are these combatants mounted, swimming or in an Ocean Location?
checks: Apply the appropriate Cavalry/cyclist/skier/boat-Passenger modifiers and Melee exemptions. Mounted status is not erased at combat start.
In allowed Water Obstacles boat Passengers fight, but the boat is not a separate CC target; it is destroyed with all its Passengers or captured by capturing them.
Swimmers have their unarmed Personnel factor and no CCV. CC is not allowed in non-frozen Ocean Locations; do not generalize river combat to surf.
options.effect: Select the actual transport/terrain profile before offering attack arithmetic.
options.example: Boat passengers in a river can fight, while non-frozen Ocean occupants cannot use the same attack.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Keep a Goliath’s special detonation option
options.prompt: Does an eligible controller have a legal detonation opportunity?
checks: A Goliath has sequential CC and can attack in its sequential window by controller detonation. Apply its own control, target and explosion rules.
It cannot be captured in CC. Do not treat the general ban on ordinary SW use as eliminating this explicit equipment exception.
options.effect: Expose a pending equipment-specific option when the scenario includes the device.
options.example: A surviving Goliath can detonate at its turn in the sequence if its controller remains eligible.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Attempt a German ATMM check
options.prompt: Would the ATMM chance justify the risk of pinning the attacker?
checks: For eligible 1944-45 German Infantry, declare the vehicle attack before the availability dr. Exclude pinned/broken units and wagon/motorcycle targets.
Success supplies -3 to that attack; apply HS/crew +1, SMC +2, CX +1 and non-armored-target +1. Leadership/heroism does not modify the check.
Original 6 pins even a berserk unit and changes CCV. Only one combined participant attempts the check; Original attack DR 12 negates the ATMM modifier.
options.effect: Show the success benefit and check-failure consequence without allowing post-check retargeting.
options.example: The squad fails its ATMM check with Original 6 and must resolve its declared attack with the new Pin penalty.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Use the T-H Hero’s distinct ATMM procedure
options.prompt: Does this unpinned hero attempt its special ATMM check?
checks: Final dr ≤3 succeeds, with only the pre-1944 +1 drm; Original 6 does not Pin this hero. Other Japanese units cannot use this permission.
If paired, the hero adds one FP/CCV to its partner and may contribute its ATMM modifier under the combined-attack rule; its standalone CCV is five.
options.effect: Use the hero-specific check rather than the German modifier list.
options.example: A pre-1944 T-H Hero has a different availability modifier and avoids the German Original-6 Pin result.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Offer eligible Hara-Kiri before a capture attempt resolves
options.prompt: Does the Japanese defender choose this immediate response?
checks: Offer immediately before a CC Capture attempt resolves, even after declaring its own attack, but not after it has already made that attack.
Berserk/heroic units may eliminate themselves automatically; otherwise resolve the NTC with the specified Inexperienced/Unarmed and paired-SMC modifiers. Best SMC acts first.
Failure forfeits that unit’s CC attack and benefits the capture attempt by the specified extra -1. Apply the appropriate VP and casualty-tally consequences on success.
options.effect: Switch decision ownership to the affected Japanese player at the exact response window.
options.example: A failed attempt can both cancel the defender’s attack and make its capture easier.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Resolve the committed attack and target-specific results
options.prompt: Which declared strength and modifier set applies to this roll?
checks: Ordinary Personnel CC below the Kill Number eliminates; equality causes Casualty Reduction through Random Selection, including ties; above normally has no effect.
Keep capture equality’s defender choice separate. Preserve Original, Final and colored-die values for special triggers.
In simultaneous CC keep already-declared attacks despite casualties. In sequential CC apply changes before offering the next declaration.
options.effect: Render a result receipt that explains each target outcome and remaining obligations.
options.example: One mixed attack can affect withdrawing and standing defenders differently.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Resolve vehicle destruction, burning or immobilization
options.prompt: What does the Final vehicle-attack DR do?
checks: Below CCV eliminates the vehicle; at or below half CCV makes a burning wreck; equality immobilizes it.
Vehicle destruction eliminates PRC without a crew-survival roll. Apply immobilization and burning consequences before subsequent attacks.
Do not use the Personnel Partial Kill rule or its Random Selection for this result.
options.effect: Show the vehicle result independently of Personnel odds.
options.example: An initial immobilization improves the conditions for a later attack against the same vehicle.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Offer the Original-2 Unlikely Kill follow-up
options.prompt: Does this Original 2 give a further vehicle-result chance?
checks: The attacker may roll the subsequent die: 1 burns, 2 eliminates, 3 immobilizes, otherwise no additional effect.
Retain any elimination/immobilization already earned by the Original attack; the follow-up cannot worsen that result, but can improve it.
Resolve the associated Infiltration and eligible Field Promotion consequences in their proper order rather than treating the extra die as the whole result.
options.effect: Show the existing guaranteed result before offering the optional improving die.
options.example: An attack that already immobilized the tank keeps that result even if the extra die has no effect.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Apply Original-12 crew small arms and ATMM consequences
options.prompt: Does this failed vehicle attack also harm the attackers?
checks: Original 12 against a non-Abandoned crewed vehicle that is neither Shocked nor Stunned causes Casualty Reduction to its attackers.
Resolve the ATMM malfunction rule and each eligible casualty/wound procedure. Do not treat a high Final DR alone as the Original-12 trigger.
options.effect: Keep self-inflicted consequences visible even when the vehicle was not harmed.
options.example: A squad’s Original 12 can reduce it despite doing nothing to the tank.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Offer immediate Infiltration withdrawal
options.prompt: Does this Original 2 or 12 open an immediate escape?
checks: An eligible Infantry/Cavalry attacker rolling Original 2 may withdraw immediately after its attack; eligible targets of Original 12 may likewise withdraw after that attack.
Respect already eliminated/captured/pinned status and the restrictions of the relevant unit profile. Do not allow the choice to be saved until its own attack or later results.
Resolve the Accessible destination, portage and movement consequences through the proper Withdrawal rules.
options.effect: Pause combat for the entitled player’s use-or-decline decision.
options.example: A target of Original 12 cannot make its pending attack and then claim the earlier Infiltration escape.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Resolve a possible CC Field Promotion
options.prompt: Did an attacking MMC roll Original 2?
checks: Use the Leader Creation table, nationality/status and attack conditions, including applicable CC-versus-AFV modifier. Apply national exceptions rather than creating a leader universally.
A created leader cannot be refused. Unless Infiltration removed the units, recompute both attacks with their original rolls, new FP/leadership and required defending association.
Do not reroll attacks or omit the creation opportunity merely because the target was a vehicle.
options.effect: Link the creation result to any required recalculation of already displayed combat.
options.example: A newly created leader can change an attack result without changing the dice already rolled.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Resolve eliminated possessors’ SW and Gun fate
options.prompt: Which equipment survives the loss of its possessor?
checks: When the Original colored CC die is 1, check each SW/Gun of an eliminated possessor with the subsequent dr against the black Kill Number.
Other equipment remains unpossessed; captured units first abandon SW. Do not automatically assign a captured weapon to the victor or use red HtH numbers for the destruction check.
options.effect: Keep equipment-loss rolls separate from casualty and capture results.
options.example: Winning HtH does not automatically destroy the defeated squad’s MG.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Reconcile simultaneous captures after both sides resolve
options.prompt: Did the capturing force survive to keep its prisoners?
checks: If a side is completely eliminated/captured in simultaneous CC, its captures in that Location during the phase are ineffective.
Apply the special mutual-elimination/capture rule for remaining unarmed prisoners, rearming and any newly opposing armed units in Melee.
Do not finalize prisoner ownership, VP or freedom after only the first side’s roll.
options.effect: Mark captures provisional until the simultaneous exchange is settled.
options.example: A squad apparently captures its opponent, but its own simultaneous elimination can undo that capture.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Assign Guards and resolve escape or rearming
options.prompt: Who guards surviving prisoners, and which escaped units become armed?
checks: Assign a legal Guard and capacity, including replacement when a Guard is eliminated. An unbroken Guard squad may use its automatic Deployment permission.
Guard attack FP versus non-prisoners is halved, not its defense. A CC attack on a Guard does not also attack its prisoners.

Escaping requires the specified absence of enemies or successful Withdrawal/Infiltration. Apply rearming by eliminated/captured armed enemy and the escaped-SMC rule; no free Scrounging action occurs here.
options.effect: Track Guard identity, capacity, escape, rearming and VP as distinct consequences.
options.example: Eliminating a broken Guard may leave prisoners in Melee with another enemy unit rather than free to leave.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Resolve successful Withdrawal and hidden-enemy entry
options.prompt: Did the withdrawing subject survive and reach a legal endpoint?
checks: For ordinary Melee Withdrawal, elimination, reduction or capture prevents successful departure. Use the particular exception for Ambush or Infiltration rather than applying all ordinary attack penalties.
Apply ≤IPC, normal advance accessibility, difficult terrain and Known-enemy exclusion. A real concealed enemy destination causes elimination and the prescribed reveal.
Record arrival and concealment effects only after origin hazards permit departure; never pre-disclose hidden occupants through route validation.
options.effect: Use a movement receipt tied to the actual withdrawal type.
options.example: A secretly occupied escape destination can eliminate the withdrawing unit despite a successful combat escape.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Resolve the Street Fighting return choice
options.prompt: Return to the origin building or remain in the road?
checks: Offer the return tied to eligible Street Fighting provenance after the applicable CC attack; do not treat it as ordinary Melee Withdrawal.
Broken, pinned or above-Wire subjects cannot return. Resolve mines/FFE normally on the return and preserve the resulting encounter state.
options.effect: Show the actual original Location and its movement consequences.
options.example: A Street Fighter can choose to stay beside the vehicle rather than return, if otherwise eligible.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Resolve FFE and mines against withdrawing subjects
options.prompt: Which attacks occur on this departure or entry?
checks: Resolve each applicable existing FFE/mine attack against the withdrawing unit/stack only. Stationary occupants are not attacked again because someone moves.
Exit mines resolve in the origin; a disabling result can prevent arrival and destination discovery. Apply entry mines only after successful exit.
Keep Harassing Fire, Barrage, Rocket, naval and terrain exceptions available. No new artillery mission action or ordinary defensive-fire window is created.
options.effect: Interleave hazards with each withdrawal rather than batch them after combat closes.
options.example: A unit survives CC but is stopped by an exit mine attack before reaching its intended cover.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Check Panji, trip flares and Column Disbandment
options.prompt: Does this actual movement or attack trigger a special effect?
checks: Apply Panji crossing and stack rules with their listed exemptions; do not assume every withdrawal is exempt simply because normal advance can be.
Resolve trip-flare activation at the triggering event. A flare activated in CCPh survives until the next Player Turn’s AFPh.
Check Column Disbandment after relevant attacks/movement using E11.532 and the special E11.533 proximity rule; ASOP’s reference to .533 does not replace the general trigger.
options.effect: Attach the special event and its future expiry to the movement receipt.
options.example: A successful withdrawal sets off a flare that must remain after this turn’s night cleanup.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Restore eligible berserk units after eliminating their enemies
options.prompt: Has this berserk unit eliminated all Known enemy units here, including at least one?
checks: Apply the stated elimination condition and restore Good Order when required; mere absence of an enemy at the start does not establish the trigger.
Keep Dare-Death voluntary-berserk recovery and T-H Hero removal separate. Recompute subsequent legal actions and closing Melee using the resulting state.
options.effect: Explain why berserk status ends or remains before the Location closes.
options.example: A berserk unit that eliminates its last Known opponent can return to normal before the next Location is selected.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Continue the sequential loop or finish the exchange
options.prompt: Does an entitled side still have an unused legal attack?
checks: Complete casualties, capture responses, Infiltration and other immediate effects before reopening 8.21B for the next attack.
Recompute targets, escorts, weapon use and ownership of the next decision. Do not reset spent attacks or allow already eliminated units to act.
options.effect: Show the next owner and remaining attacks rather than a generic Next button.
options.example: After an escort is eliminated, the next attacker sees the tank’s revised protection.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Resolve Interrogation when the optional rule is in use
options.prompt: Is this a new eligible prisoner under the active rules profile?
checks: When E2 is in use, apply the immediate one-DR-per-prisoner procedure; a failed or unusable result does not permit another roll for that prisoner.
Apply prisoner/Guard and nationality/scenario modifiers, including Japanese 1944-45 and Chinese allegiance provisions.
Apply only the required disclosure, valid fallback result and prisoner-side tie choice. Do not reveal hidden positions to both clients while calculating privately.
options.effect: Record the prisoner’s interrogated status and the authorized information change.
options.example: A prisoner with no usable first result cannot be interrogated again after the next attack.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Capture eligible unescorted abandoned vehicles
options.prompt: Is automatic capture now allowed after this Location’s combat?
checks: If the conditions are met, assign the capturing Infantry and vehicle ownership at Location close. No extra Ambush roll is made against an abandoned vehicle alone.
Apply temporary driver/crew consequences, including a squad’s exchange for a HS and SMC restrictions; do not hand out a fully qualified free crew.
Preserve captured-use, movement and VP requirements for later phases. Current coverage includes capture foundations, but remaining detailed consequences stay labeled.
options.effect: Show who becomes the crew and which Infantry remains outside.
options.example: Capturing an armed vehicle consumes the proper capturing manpower rather than duplicating it.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Determine Melee per surviving unit
options.prompt: Who is actually held, who holds the enemy, and who remains free?
checks: Retained concealment neither holds nor is held in Melee. Vehicles are never held, but qualifying non-Abandoned unbroken Stopped vehicles can hold Known enemy Infantry.
Apply mobile/immobile PRC, Cavalry/cyclist/skier, sewer and pillbox exceptions. Do not mark every surviving counter identically.
Flip/remove CC or retain/remove Melee as appropriate; carry future movement/fire restrictions to the next turn.
options.effect: Record a per-unit hold reason rather than one blanket Location flag.
options.example: A stopped tank holds enemy Infantry even though the tank itself is free to move in its next MPh.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: End voluntary Dare-Death berserk status when permitted
options.prompt: Does this voluntarily berserk unit remain in Melee?
checks: Voluntarily berserk Dare-Death participants return to normal at turn end unless still in Melee; preserve provenance rather than treating every berserk result alike.
Retain applicable Dare-Death CC attributes even when no longer berserk. Resolve ordinary A15.46 recovery separately.
options.effect: Show the rule and state that preserve or remove this specific berserk marker.
options.example: A voluntary Dare-Death unit outside Melee recovers, while one still held remains berserk.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Remove spent Tank-Hunter Heroes at their rule window
options.prompt: Has the hero completed its permitted CC attack?
checks: Remove a non-hidden T-H Hero immediately after its CC attack against its Designated Target. If it makes no such attack, remove it at the end of its creation/HIP-loss Player Turn unless held in Melee; then remove it when freed. Earlier loss of the Designated Target eliminates it immediately.
Preserve related DC/equipment and VP rules. Do not use the general Melee-survivor routine to keep it in play.
options.effect: Carry the hero-specific expiry through the attack and Location closing record.
options.example: A surviving T-H Hero attack does not imply the hero remains for another turn.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.
options.timing: Immediately after its Designated-Target attack; otherwise G1.425 turn-end/Melee continuation

options.title: Declare Dogfight groups and initial targets
options.prompt: Which eligible aircraft enter combat, and what is each first target?
checks: Only an undamaged FB voluntarily initiates Aerial Combat. Form the allowed aircraft groups and account for existing Aerial Melee.
Predesignate every aircraft’s initial target, ATTACKER first, before results. Despite sequential resolution, an aircraft cannot wait to pick its initial target.
Resolve all ATTACKER attacks, including retained ROF, before surviving DEFENDER return attacks.
options.effect: Use a distinct aerial declaration receipt rather than the ground CC alternation rule.
options.example: A second fighter cannot change its declared first target because the first fighter destroyed another plane.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Resolve aerial attacks, damage and retained ROF
options.prompt: What does this attack do, and may the FB attack again?
checks: Apply the aerial modifiers and table: Final DR ≤4 eliminates; 5 Damages. A second Damage eliminates; surviving damaged aircraft face Recall/Aerial Melee rules.
FB ROF is 1 with bombs or 2 without. A retained-ROF follow-up may choose another target in its Dogfight, after its required initial attack.
Original 12 disables MG; Original 11 by a FB attacking a Stuka invokes its special rear-gunner result. Do not use ground CC Infiltration or Field Promotion.
options.effect: Display aircraft-specific outcomes and remaining ROF before return fire.
options.example: A fighter retains ROF and can select another plane after resolving its declared initial target.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Choose Recall and determine continuing Aerial Melee
options.prompt: Which aircraft must leave, may leave, or remain held?
checks: A Final attack DR ≥10 gives its target an end-CCPh Recall option. Damaged or MG-disabled aircraft have their own Recall and enemy-FB constraints.
Continuing Aerial Melee requires a qualifying undamaged FB with functioning MG wishing to hold opponents. Ordinary Infantry Withdrawal rules do not apply.
Bomb jettison is a separate own-MPh option, not a late CCPh way to alter already declared attacks.
options.effect: Resolve each aircraft’s exit decision and next-turn hold status.
options.example: A damaged bomber may be held in Aerial Melee rather than automatically disappearing at once.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Validate pending non-Flame Clearance tasks
options.prompt: Which earlier declarations remain eligible to resolve now?
checks: Use the carried declaration, target and participants from the proper MPh/DFPh window. Pin or loss of Good Order can end participation.
Combine attempts against the same item in the same phase as required; apply task-specific leadership, Sapper, Hero, dozer and Labor modifiers.
Do not offer a fresh uncommitted task or resolve Flame Clearance here. Resolve tasks before ordinary TI/Pin cleanup.
options.effect: Make the declaration’s history and current eligibility visible.
options.example: A pinned clearing squad cannot regain eligibility by clearing Pin early.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Complete rubble or roadblock Clearance
options.prompt: Which terrain change does a successful task create?
checks: Rubble Clearance in a qualifying non-building hex places a TB through chosen hexsides, preserving terrain LOS/TEM until complete removal conditions are met.
Roadblock Clearance removes the specified obstacle; use the correct earlier declaration and eligible Infantry/dozer path rather than treating both tasks as identical.
options.effect: Preview the affected hexsides and exact surviving terrain.
options.example: A cleared rubble lane lowers entry cost along its TB without instantly removing all rubble TEM.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Complete Wire or Set DC Clearance
options.prompt: Did the qualified clearing party retain the required position and status?
checks: Wire removal requires the prescribed below-Wire position and prior task commitment. Being above Wire is not enough.
Set DC removal has its own same-Location declaration and eligibility. Resolve the Clearance result; do not detonate or Recover the device as a substitute.
options.effect: Keep target identity and above/below status in the task record.
options.example: A squad below Wire can finish its declared removal while a squad above it cannot assist as though colocated.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Resolve Infantry minefield lanes and mishaps
options.prompt: Does the task establish a safe lane, or cause casualties?
checks: Resolve the committed mine Clearance and any Sapper benefit. On success place the legal TB including a previously established partial TB hexside.
Original 12, or 11-12 for Inexperienced clearers, causes the specified Casualty Reduction. Preserve the partial lane’s user/exit limitations until a full result exists.
Only when every hexside is crossed by TB does full removal occur; a single success is not blanket minefield deletion.
options.effect: Show lane geometry and casualty risk independently of the success total.
options.example: A failed task can leave its entering unit a special exit without making that route safe for everyone.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Resolve a Flail Tank’s special mine Clearance
options.prompt: Did the Flail Tank complete the qualifying movement and remain eligible?
checks: Require the proper entire-MPh commitment, no disqualifying fire/immobility/elimination and no friendly Infantry/Cavalry/vulnerable PRC in the minefield.
Use its special Final DR ≤10 and legal entry-hexside-to-current-VCA TB. Original 11 destroys the mechanism; Original 12 has the A-T/A-P-specific destruction or immobilization result.
options.effect: Use a separate vehicle procedure rather than the Infantry ≤2 target.
options.example: A tank can survive while losing its flail mechanism and future Clearance ability.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Complete jungle/bamboo paths or Panji Clearance
options.prompt: Which path or Covered hexside was the declared target?
checks: Path creation uses its restricted armed MMC eligibility and dedicated modifier list, including light jungle, bamboo and CX, not the generic extra-manpower benefits.
Panji Clearance changes a predesignated Covered hexside to non-Covered using Wire-like procedures. Units above Panji cannot attempt, direct or assist either task.
Preserve the chosen path hexsides and remaining obstacle state.
options.effect: Show path creation and Panji hexside removal as distinct effects.
options.example: A successful Panji task opens one predesignated hexside rather than deleting the entire counter.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Keep debris and dozer-specific task profiles available
options.prompt: Does this scenario add a specialized pending task?
checks: ASOP explicitly includes O1.5 Debris Clearance. Preserve it as a separate selectable profile with its source verification status; do not silently treat Debris as rubble.
Dozer terrain/fortification/cave tasks use their own prior commitments, mobility, Melee and result requirements. An unsupported profile must remain visible as pending.
Require the scenario/module source and task-specific result before a live execution is offered.
options.effect: Keep named source gaps distinct from absent engine support.
options.example: A Red Barricades debris task remains represented even when the current rules package cannot execute it.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Update Labor after an unsuccessful eligible task
options.prompt: Does this failure establish or improve the task’s Labor status?
checks: Apply the -1 then -2 progression to that same task; new participants can join a continuing task under the rule.
Remove Labor when the task succeeds or all relevant MMC are eliminated/leave. Do not carry the benefit to a different target or treat every phase without an attempt as a failure.
options.effect: Attach Labor to the task and its surviving work party.
options.example: A failed Wire task does not grant a bonus to clearing nearby mines.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Resolve destruction of Recovered tunnel entrances
options.prompt: Which entrance has been lawfully discovered and can be destroyed?
checks: Require the used-in-LOS and subsequent Recovery discovery history, eligible Good Order Infantry and no Known enemy in its Location.
The ASOP places Recovered-entrance elimination here; preserve B8.63’s eligibility and destruction permission. Do not reveal entrances merely because a Search happened nearby.
options.effect: Show the discovered entrance and qualified destruction decision before removing it.
options.example: An unrecovered secret tunnel is not deleted by a generic end-turn cleanup.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Remove Pin and ordinary TI after tasks resolve
options.prompt: Which markers expire now, and which belong to continuing tasks?
checks: Remove the appropriate Pin and ordinary TI markers only after combat and Clearance windows finish.

Do not remove Ammo Replenishment TI prematurely or Animal-Pack counters. Retain their multi-turn task history and later completion windows. Classify Pin markers by their cause: LC-Blaze Pin follows G12.68, and new/Hampered Flame markers carry terrain history rather than personnel status.
options.effect: Use a rule-owned expiry list, not a blanket remove-all-status command.
options.example: The clearing squad loses ordinary TI, but a Gun being Animal-Packed remains Pack-TI.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Convert Stun while preserving cumulative effects
options.prompt: Which Stun flips to a lasting penalty, and which uses a cumulative profile?
checks: Flip ordinary Stun to its +1 side at the proper time; do not erase the penalty or equate this with a free CE change.
Apply LC and seaborne cumulative-Stun exceptions. Preserve Recall and crew consequences under the applicable vehicle profile.
options.effect: Explain recovery of immediate capabilities separately from retained penalties.
options.example: An AFV’s Stun expires as an immediate restriction while its +1 remains.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Complete or continue Ammo Replenishment
options.prompt: Has the required number of complete Game Turns been maintained?
checks: Check qualifying locations, compatible ammunition, uninterrupted TI and CE, and the B#-dependent duration. Moving, firing, losing CE or being attacked in CC can interrupt the process.
On completion restore the allowed depleted ammunition and make the Ammo Vehicle’s exhaustion DR. Original 12 removes its supply role.
Retain incomplete-task TI and separate any Ammo Dump/transfer completion. Do not count an interrupted partial Game Turn as complete.
options.effect: Show completed turns, interruption cause and the next required outcome.
options.example: An attack in CC can interrupt resupply even if it causes no casualties.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Evaluate eligible ATTACKER concealment gain
options.prompt: Which units qualify now under the governing concealment table?
checks: Use the unit category, Good Order status, Concealment Terrain, enemy LOS and range; the Concealment Table controls over generic prose.
Evaluate unbroken enemy observers, including the proper Dummy/vehicle distinctions. Apply the lawful disclosure rule if a hidden unit is used to deny concealment.
Only the appropriate ATTACKER units gain concealment here. Do not grant new HIP or regain Cloaking as an ordinary end-turn benefit.
options.effect: Show authorized reasons for automatic gain, a required dr, or refusal without secret-state leakage.
options.example: An eligible unit outside enemy LOS can gain concealment while a broken unit cannot.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Make each required concealment dr
options.prompt: Does this unit need a roll instead of automatic gain?
checks: Use the two specified terrain/range/LOS cases. Roll separately for each qualifying unit, with success on Final dr ≤5.
Apply US#, valid leadership, Lax/Stealthy, terrain/Hindrance and Japanese modifiers. A stack does not share one all-or-nothing result.
Use the night automatic-gain exception when applicable rather than rolling unnecessarily.
options.effect: Show per-unit outcomes and the source of each modifier.
options.example: A squad can fail while its leader and Hero in the same stack qualify.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.

options.title: Apply night, winter, desert and campaign concealment rules
options.prompt: Which special profile modifies ordinary concealment gain?
checks: Night makes daylight dr cases automatic; winter camouflage, desert visibility and Japanese modifiers require their own applicable conditions.
Retain named ABtF CG12, BRT CG11, KGP CG11, PB CG10 and RB CG15 profiles from ASOP, with source gaps explicitly identified until those campaign rules are reconciled.
A cave’s entry-based HIP permission is not an end-CCPh HIP gain. Do not promise every module’s concealment behavior from the generic table.
options.effect: Keep profile options available while distinguishing verified rules from missing scenario evidence.
options.example: A campaign concealment exception remains selectable for study even before its module source is integrated.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Remove Starshells and IR after concealment is assessed
options.prompt: Which illumination expires at this Player Turn’s end?
checks: Evaluate concealment gain first, with the illumination still present. Then remove all Starshells and IR at this window.
Do not clear Blazes, Flames, every trip flare or active searchlights merely because they also illuminate. Their removal rules differ.
options.effect: Show ordered expiry so darkness cannot grant premature concealment.
options.example: A Starshell still affects the concealment decision before it is removed.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Remove night Acquisition that loses illumination
options.prompt: Does the target retain the required Blaze/Flame illumination?
checks: At turn end retain Acquisition only under the specified Blaze/Flame illumination condition. Starshell/IR expiry can remove its supporting illumination.
Respect the broader immediate-loss rule whenever illumination disappears earlier. Do not treat all Acquisition as expiring every turn or preserve it because the Gun is still present.
options.effect: Link each Acquisition expiry to its target’s illumination state.
options.example: A target illuminated only by IR loses Acquisition when that IR expires.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.

options.title: Expire cave smoke and resolve connected WP disclosures
options.prompt: Does a half-inch SMOKE counter in a cave expire at this turn’s end?
checks: Half-inch SMOKE placed in a cave persists until the end of that Player Turn. Apply the specified expiry after concealment placement; do not clear every ordnance SMOKE counter by the same rule.
Removing cave WP can immediately reveal higher connected hidden caves and above-ground tunnel openings under G11.851, regardless of LOS. Determine the exact Accessible/Complex relationships.
Revealing a tunnel opening in a hidden pillbox does not reveal the pillbox itself. Keep the required disclosure narrower than a blanket reveal of all underground contents.
options.effect: Attach connected revelation to the WP expiry event.
options.example: A cave WP counter expires and reveals a higher tunnel opening while the pillbox containing it remains hidden.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.
options.timing: Rule-specific CCPh timing; supplemental to ASOP

options.title: Remove a landing-craft Blaze’s temporary Pin marker
options.prompt: Which newly placed Blaze has reached its next-CCPh expiry?
checks: A Blaze placed on a LC initially receives a Pin marker. Remove that marker at the end of the next CCPh according to its placement record, without extinguishing the Blaze.
Preserve duplicate Passenger-wreck bookkeeping. The unpinned Blaze then has its specified MP and later AFPh damage effects; those are not a fresh CCPh attack.
options.effect: Distinguish a fire-timing marker from a pinned Personnel unit.
options.example: Removing the marker activates the Blaze’s later effects rather than clearing the fire.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.
options.timing: Rule-specific CCPh timing; supplemental to ASOP

options.title: Remove only the trip flares due now
options.prompt: Was this flare activated during MPh or during a later phase?
checks: Red-on-white MPh trip flares expire at the end of that Player Turn’s CCPh after concealment placement.
Purple-on-white RtPh/APh/CCPh flares persist until the next Player Turn’s AFPh. Store activation provenance, not just a generic flare flag.
options.effect: Use an expiry record tied to the activation phase.
options.example: A flare triggered by this CCPh’s Withdrawal survives when the older MPh flare is removed.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.
options.timing: Rule-specific CCPh timing; supplemental to ASOP

options.title: Resolve check-triggered effects without inventing Sniper activity
options.prompt: Does a required check trigger a separate rule effect?
checks: Apply Booby Trap and casualty/wound consequences to qualifying checks under the scenario profile; preserve Original dice and proper Random Selection.
Ordinary CCPh rolls are not among A14.1’s normal SAN phases. Do not run a generic Sniper trigger on every CC or task-check roll.
Preserve Field Promotion and special Original-2/12 branches instead of hiding them behind the ordinary attack result.
options.effect: Expose only the triggered branch supported by its rule.
options.example: An escape NTC can need a Booby Trap check without creating an ordinary CCPh Sniper attack.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.
options.timing: Rule-specific CCPh timing; supplemental to ASOP

options.title: Finish obligations and hand over the Player Turn
options.prompt: Is every Location and phase-wide continuation settled?
checks: Require completion of all selected Locations, aerial choices, declared tasks, required status changes, concealment and night expiries before the turn changes.
Carry Melee, HtH, Guard/crew identities, captured equipment, Labor, ongoing resupply/Pack-TI and future flare expiries into the next turn.
Do not clear DM/CX or every fire/status marker through a generic CCPh cleanup. Use each marker’s rule and apply scenario victory timing separately.
options.effect: Keep End Location, End ground combat and End Player Turn distinct in the live design.
options.example: No ground fights remain, but incomplete resupply and a next-turn flare still require carried state.
options.status: Partially integrated; full rule path remains to be verified.
options.timing: Rule-specific CCPh timing; supplemental to ASOP

options.title: Preserve all identified options and source boundaries
options.prompt: Which rules are verified, which await integration, and which need more source evidence?
checks: All 17 printed CCPh steps and identified supplemental families are represented. This is not certification of every Chapter H note, historical module, SSR or optional combination.
Keep pending integration, source gaps, unknown applicability and known illegality separate. Missing evaluators must not hide reference choices.
The future Blazor guide should consume viewer-safe Rules projections and durable decision receipts. This preview neither adjudicates combat nor implements engine passes.
options.effect: Expose source and integration limitations without shrinking the intended completed system.
options.example: A deferred sN attack remains visible with its prerequisites even when the current engine cannot execute it.
options.status: Rules integration pending; reference available.
options.timing: Rule-specific CCPh timing; supplemental to ASOP

glossary.CCPh: Close Combat Phase. Resolve each selected Location completely, then resolve phase-wide aerial combat, Clearance and cleanup.
glossary.CC: Close Combat. Usually simultaneous attacks between opposing units in a Location, with explicit sequencing, vehicle and terrain exceptions.
glossary.Melee: Continuing combat status determined per eligible unit after the Location’s combat, with concealment, vehicle, transport, sewer and pillbox exceptions.
glossary.Declaration receipt: Proposed live record of attackers, defending groups, targets, attack mode, strength, modifiers and obligations at the commitment boundary.
glossary.Location: A hex can contain multiple Locations. Same hex does not necessarily mean a leader can help or a transfer is legal.
glossary.PRC: Passengers, Riders and Crew, with different vulnerability and fire restrictions.
glossary.HIP: Hidden Initial Placement. No guide prompt may leak hidden opposing information.
glossary.T-H Hero: Japanese Tank-Hunter Hero, created through G1.421 with a Designated Target and special compulsory advance and combat rules.
glossary.Ambush: An opening advantage that can change attack order, CC DRM, concealment and withdrawal. It is not rerolled merely because new units reinforce a Melee.
glossary.dr: One-die roll. Ambush and ATMM use dr, not DR.
glossary.drm: Modifier to a one-die roll, such as an Ambush or ATMM check.
glossary.CX: Counter Exhausted. Usually bars an already-CX unit from a difficult advance; climbing and deep-stream entry have explicit exceptions. A difficult advance creates CX.
glossary.BU: Buttoned Up. The alternative protected crew posture, with weapon and observation consequences.
glossary.Stealthy: A11.17 quality affecting Ambush and other named checks, subject to Good Order, nationality and Lax exceptions.
glossary.Withdrawal: Leaving combat under a specific rule. Ordinary Melee Withdrawal, Ambush Withdrawal, Infiltration and Street Fighting return have different eligibility and timing.
glossary.Street Fighting: A11.8 vehicle combat advantage and return option based on eligible road/building or Bypass relationships, distinct from an actual Ambush.
glossary.Designated Target: The qualifying target chosen when a T-H Hero appears. It constrains the hero’s subsequent actions.
glossary.Sequential CC: Attacks resolved in order, with the next declaration allowed after earlier results. Eliminated units lose their pending attack opportunities.
glossary.Simultaneous CC: Both sides declare before resolution. A declared attack still resolves at its original strength despite simultaneous elimination, reduction or capture, subject to explicit interrupts.
glossary.Prisoners: Captured Personnel under a Guard. Transfer, abandonment, accompaniment and escape have distinct rule windows.
glossary.Guard: Unit assigned to prisoners. Capacity, fire restrictions and accompaniment are separate from the act of accepting surrender.
glossary.NTC: Normal Task Check, used only when the governing rule calls for it.
glossary.Personnel Escort: Qualified Personnel in the vehicle’s Location that modify its vulnerability, assessed at each attack rather than frozen for the whole phase.
glossary.CCV: Close Combat Value. Used for Personnel attacking vehicles and as the defending strength against vehicle CC fire. It is not the unit’s printed Infantry FP.
glossary.SMC: Single-Man Counter, such as a leader or Hero.
glossary.Disrupted: A19.12 status with its own opening surrender and restricted rout rules. Ordinary daytime Low Crawl is unavailable; night and No Quarter require explicit treatment.
glossary.IPC: Inherent Portage Capacity. Evaluate retained load and eligible leader assistance before the difficult-advance test.
glossary.PP: Portage Points. A retained load leaving no MF bars advance even into otherwise inexpensive terrain.
glossary.Accessible: A rules-defined connection usable by hypothetical Infantry under normal advance conditions, ignoring enemy presence. Special cave and terrain restrictions still apply.
glossary.MMC: Multi-Man Counter: squad, half-squad or crew.
glossary.DRM: Modifier to a two-dice roll. Keep target-specific CC modifiers separate from Ambush one-die modifiers.
glossary.CCT: Close Combat Table. Personnel odds use its appropriate black or Hand-to-Hand red Kill Numbers; personnel attacks on vehicles instead use CCV.
glossary.HtH: Hand-to-Hand CC. Uses red Kill Numbers when the applicable nationality, Deluxe or SSR rule permits or requires it. Not a universal choice.
glossary.Dare-Death: Chinese designated MMC with special HtH/non-HtH benefits and voluntary-berserk recovery rules.
glossary.Partial Kill: Final CC DR equal to the applicable Kill Number. Ordinary attacks use Random Selection for Casualty Reduction; capture has its own selection procedure.
glossary.No Quarter: A surrender policy under A20.3. It does not create a generic right to replace every CC capture with elimination.
glossary.RMG: Rear Machine Gun. Use its eligible CC FP under A11.62; weapon allocation remains distinct from ordinary fire.
glossary.IFE: Infantry Firepower Equivalent, a weapon-specific alternative to ordinary TH fire.
glossary.sN: Nahverteidigungswaffe. A qualifying BU AFV’s separate close-defense HE attack on the IFT, with usage and timing restrictions and friendly-unit exposure.
glossary.Pillbox: Separate Location equivalent to a building for rout, with special Known-enemy, entry/exit, ordinary forced-rout and Blaze rules.
glossary.Wire: Obstacle with distinct above/below states. Infantry cannot move beneath it during APh.
glossary.Panji: Covered-hexside obstacle. Normal advance avoids its entry MC; difficult advance can trigger it. APh does not permit the extra-MF move beneath it.
glossary.Skis: E4 equipment whose mode changes and downhill bonus have explicit RtPh permission. Low Crawl requires removing skis.
glossary.ATMM: Anti-Tank Magnetic Mine. A pre-resolution availability check after declaring the attack, with nationality/date and failure rules; it is not ordinary fire.
glossary.Hara-Kiri: G1.641 Japanese Personnel self-elimination attempt immediately before a CC Capture attempt resolves, with special eligibility, order and failure consequences.
glossary.DR: Two-dice roll. Preserve Original and Final values and the colored die for special results.
glossary.Wound: A17 injury with severity, reduced morale/leadership, IPC and movement consequences. Track MF already spent if it occurs mid-rout.
glossary.Infiltration: Immediate withdrawal opportunity from an Original CC DR of 2 or 12, with eligibility restrictions. It cannot be saved until after another attack.
glossary.SW: Support Weapon. Using one affects its possessor’s capability accounting.
glossary.FFE: Fire For Effect. Existing HE/WP FFE can attack the routing subject on qualifying entry or increased vulnerability; it does not itself Interdict.
glossary.WP: White Phosphorus, with its own height, NMC and ignition rules.
glossary.Trip Flare: E1.95 hidden device with entry/expenditure triggers. A flare set off in RtPh persists until the next Player Turn’s AFPh cleanup.
glossary.Column: Formation using multi-hex Impulse movement/advance at its slowest unit’s rate, with restrictions and immediate Disbandment checks.
glossary.Good Order: The defined unit status, separate from merely unbroken. Apply the exact status requirement of each action.
glossary.Interrogation: E2 optional-rule procedure, when in use, immediately after capture or surrender. One roll per prisoner, with controlled disclosure.
glossary.Dogfight: Aerial-combat group with predesignated initial targets, ATTACKER-first sequential attacks, special ROF, damage and Recall.
glossary.FB: Fighter-Bomber, an aircraft type with its own sighting and Ground Support procedures.
glossary.Aerial Melee: Continuing Dogfight held by a qualifying undamaged FB with functioning MG. Ordinary Infantry Withdrawal rules do not apply.
glossary.ROF: Rate of Fire. A retained opportunity is not an automatic shot.
glossary.Clearance: Resolution of a previously declared task. Non-Flame tasks finish in CCPh under their own eligibility and result rules; this is not a fresh declaration window.
glossary.TI: Task Involved status, not a synonym for Prep Fire.
glossary.Labor: Task-specific Clearance benefit earned by failure, normally progressing from -1 to -2. It does not transfer freely to another task.
glossary.TB: Trail Break. Creation and use depend on terrain and the applicable vehicle procedure.
glossary.SSR: Scenario Special Rule. It can add or modify applicability and must be included in the scenario profile.
glossary.Tunnel: B8.62 special rout connection between entrances, with emergence conditions and immunity to Interdiction while inside.
glossary.Pack-TI: Animal-Pack task status. It survives ordinary end-CCPh TI removal and completes at its specified later Rally window.
glossary.CE: Crew Exposed. A vehicle crew posture whose voluntary changes have timing restrictions.
glossary.LOS: Line of Sight. Guidance uses only information the viewing player may know.
glossary.Cloaking: Night concealment representation whose contents normally advance as one stack until properly separated; hidden contents remain owner-only.
glossary.Source gap: Missing or unreconciled scenario/module/equipment evidence, distinct from a rule awaiting implementation.
glossary.IR: Illuminating Round, with its own usage and placement procedure.
glossary.Acquisition: A weapon-specific targeting benefit. Tracking a moving target is not permission to fire in APh.
glossary.LC: Landing Craft, governed by its own transport, fire, beaching and grounding rules.
